pool.text: A town approximately on the Belaya River was designated as Pascherti.
Ivan the Terrible ordered a fortress built on the site of modern Ufa.
Town status was granted to the location of the Russian fortress.
Ufa was made capital of Ufa Governorate when it split from Orenburg.
The Belaya River Waterway connected the city to the European Russian Empire.
The Samara-Zlatoust Railroad connected the city to the European Russian Empire.
Many industrial enterprises of the western Soviet Union were evacuated here.
The Russian Islamic University was opened in the urban area.
A train disaster occurred when a pipeline leak released gas near rails.
Forbes named the city the best place for business among large settlements.
Researchers published a paper arguing for an ancient settlement hypothesis here.
The city hosted separate summits of the BRICS group and Shanghai organization.
The maximum single concentration of suspended solids reached high levels.
The world's first monument to a tick was erected in the city center.
